A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RSPO research. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and visual inspection supports matching equations, figures, tables, and relocated content.

before.justification: V2 reports original Mistral fine-tuning experiments, regularization ablations, response-quality evaluations, and synthetic simulations.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds evaluations using LLaMA, Gemma, and a stronger preference model.

M1.justification: The modular RSPO loss, update direction, baseline, Algorithm 1, and divergence implementations in Appendix C.3 remain unchanged. The additional model evaluations and newly stated implementation assumptions do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use UltraFeedback prompts and validation data, AlpacaEval-2.0, Arena-Hard, MT-Bench, and the same synthetic scenarios. V3 expands model configurations without adding datasets, domains, or task requirements.

E2.justification: V3 Table 2 removes the standalone IS-forward-KL RSPO variant from the diversity comparison reported in v2 Table 3, although that variant remains evaluated elsewhere. The principal benchmark comparators, including SPPO, Snorkel, iterative DPO, and SimPO, are retained.

E3.justification: V2's experiments use Mistral-7B and PairRM-0.4B. V3 adds LLaMA3-8B-Instruct and Gemma2-2B-IT configurations, experiments with GPM-8B preference feedback, and model-specific regularization settings. The retained Mistral experiments still report the same prompt splits, five sampled responses, metrics, and extended SPPO iteration budget.

E4.justification: V3 adds tests of regularization across model architectures and preference-model strength, plus LLaMA ablations examining forward-KL strength and combined versus reverse-only KL regularization (Figure 4 and Tables 9–10). These test whether the Mistral findings generalize. Conversely, the forward-KL-only diversity results are removed; existing Mistral sensitivity analyses and synthetic examples remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without independent repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V3 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: The principal Mistral results are retained. Newly reported v3 comparisons give SPPO/RSPO AlpacaEval LCWRs of 38.77/43.66 for LLaMA, 50.54/51.83 for Gemma, and 44.26/44.70 for LLaMA with GPM-8B (Figure 4; Tables 7–8). Table 10 reports 41.84 for combined KL versus 43.66 for reverse-only KL on LLaMA. V2's three forward-KL-only Self-BLEU entries disappear.

T1.justification: V3 formalizes on-policy sampling as Assumption A.2 and makes Corollary 3.2 conditional on it. It adds a combined-KL relative-convexity lemma and proof, an explicit geometric KL convergence bound, and revises the RSPO–GMMD derivation. These materially extend and qualify the formal treatment. However, equation (12) replaces v2's regularizer-gradient term with R itself, inconsistent with v3 appendix equation (39).

C1.justification: The central claims about modular regularized self-play and convergence are retained. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion broaden the empirical effectiveness claim to LLaMA and Gemma and add a parameter-efficiency claim relative to SPPO using stronger preference feedback.

C2.justification: V3 explains that reverse-only KL works better on LLaMA because forward KL provides little length reduction, qualifying the Mistral-based recommendation. It adds a parameter-efficiency interpretation of the GPM comparison and explicitly qualifies theory with on-policy sampling. The empirical expressiveness limitation in v2 Appendix E.3 and detailed main-text ArmoRM interpretation are removed, while the ArmoRM results remain.

D1.justification: V3 adds a code-access link and newly describes a single optimizer update on each collected batch as making training effectively on-policy; this disclosure does not establish a change from v2's implementation. New tables specify additional model-specific regularization coefficients and clipping settings. Existing divergence implementations and A100 hardware disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: New Appendix E.4 substantially expands positioning against regularized game-solving research, including work by Abe, Perolat, Hennes, and others. It contrasts prior methods' scale and regularizer restrictions with RSPO's proposed scope. V3 also adds the GPM reference; the earlier RLHF and self-play related-work discussions largely remain.

P1.justification: V3 rewrites the abstract and contribution bullets, revises portions of the experimental and theoretical narrative, adds impact and acknowledgements text, and updates affiliations. Most method prose and the overall section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The main text and references change to a two-column layout. V2 Table 1 becomes the front-page bar-chart Figure 1, retained temperature plots are rearranged, and the ArmoRM table moves to the appendix. V3 also adds Figure 4 and Tables 7–10 and restructures the diversity table. These are substantial display and layout changes.

improvement.justification: The added model and preference-feedback evaluations address part of v2's explicitly acknowledged empirical limitation, while the LLaMA ablations clarify when combined KL is useful. Explicit assumptions, broader research positioning, and code-access information also help. These gains are partly offset by removing forward-KL diversity evidence and introducing the equation (12) gradient inconsistency, yielding a limited net improvement.
